NONE: › used when giving the name that a person is generally known by, after giving their real name
又名，亦名；化名為
› a false name, especially one used by a criminal
（尤指罪犯用的）化名，假名

example: Malcolm Little, alias Malcolm X
他名為Malcolm Litt，也稱Malcolm X。
He travels under (= using) an alias.
他使用化名旅行。

NONE: › proof that someone who is thought to have committed a crime could not have done it, especially the fact or statement that they were in another place at the time it happened
（尤指沒有犯罪時間的）不在犯罪現場的證據
› an excuse for something bad or for a failure
藉口，託辭

example: He has a cast-iron (= very strong) alibi - he was in hospital the week of the murder.
他有不在犯罪現場的鐵證——謀殺發生的那一週他在住院。
After eight years in power, the government can no longer use the previous government's policy as an alibi for its own failure.
本屆政府已經執政八年，面對自己的失敗，它再不能拿前任政府的政策作擋箭牌了。

外國的；異域的；異族的
› strange and not familiar
怪異的；截然不同的；不熟悉的
› specialized law someone who lives in a country of which they are not a legal citizen
（通常指不是所在國公民的）外國人，外僑，僑民

外星人（或生物）

example: an alien culture
異域文化
Synonym
foreign
When I first went to New York, it all felt very alien to me.
我初到紐約的時候，覺得一切都非常陌生。
an alien spacecraft
外星人飛船

戰爭爆發時，政府把數以千計的外國人集中在一起，關在臨時拘留營中。

T: › to cause someone or a group of people to stop supporting and agreeing with you
› to make someone feel that they are different and not part of a group

example: All these changes to the newspaper have alienated its traditional readers.
報紙改頭換面疏遠了老讀者。
Disagreements can alienate teenagers from their families.
家庭爭吵會使青少年跟家人產生感情裂痕。

U: › the feeling that you have no connection with the people around you
› the act of making someone stop supporting and agreeing with you

example: Depressed people frequently feel a sense of alienation from those around them.
情緒抑鬱的人經常感到與身邊的人格格不入。
This short-sighted alienation of their own supporters may lose them the election.
這種疏遠自己支持者的短視做法或許會使他們輸掉選舉。

after verb: 容光煥發的；興奮的，喜悅的

I: › [ I ] formal to get out of a vehicle, especially a train or bus
（尤指從火車或公共汽車上）下來，下去

I + adv/prep: › [ I + adv/prep ] formal to land on something
› [ I + adv/prep ] literary to find or unexpectedly see something
發現；偶然碰見；無意中發覺

example: I had to use a bit of petrol to get the fire alight.
我不得不倒了一點汽油才生著了火。
The rioters overturned several cars and set them alight.
暴徒掀翻了幾輛汽車並將其付之一炬。
He was smoking in bed and his blankets caught alight.
他在床上抽煙，把毯子點著了。
The sky was alight with hundreds of fireworks.
無數的煙花照亮了天空。
Her eyes were alight with mischief.
她的眼神裡透著調皮。
The suspect alighted from the train at Euston and proceeded to Heathrow.
嫌疑犯在尤斯頓下了火車，接著又趕往希斯洛機場。
A butterfly alighted gently on the flower.
一隻蝴蝶輕輕落在那朵花上。
As she glanced round the room her eyes alighted upon a small child.
她環視房間，目光無意中落在一個小孩身上。
I spent an hour in the bookshop before alighting on the perfect present.
我在書店裡逛了一個小時才發現這本書——當作禮物真是再合適不過了。

NONE: › to put two or more things into a straight line
使成一條直線；對準；校直

example: When you've aligned the notch on the gun with the target, fire!
當槍的標尺、準星和目標成一條直線時，開火！
Align the ruler and the middle of the paper and then cut it straight.
讓尺子對齊紙的中線，然後沿尺子剪開。

NONE: › If you align yourself with an organization or person, you agree with and support their aims.
與…保持一致；與…結盟

example: The party is under pressure to align itself more closely with industry.
該黨受壓力所迫，需要與企業界拉近關係。
The major unions are aligned with the government on this issue.
在這一問題上，幾個主要的工會立場與政府保持一致。

U: › [ U ] an arrangement in which two or more things are positioned in a straight line or parallel to each other

C: › [ C ] an agreement between a group of countries, political parties, or people who want to work together because of shared interests or aims

example: The problem is happening because the wheels are out of alignment with each other.
出現這個問題是因為車輪定位不正。
New alignments are being formed within the business community.
在商界，新的聯盟關係正逐漸形成。

NONE: B1 similar to each other
相似的，類似的；相像的
B2 in a similar way
相似地；相同地
B2 used after referring to two groups of people or things to show that both groups are included
兩者都；同樣地，同等地

example: The children all look very alike.
孩子長得都很像。
The twins even dress alike.
這對雙胞胎就連衣著都一樣。
My father treated us all alike.
父親待我們一視同仁。
Friends and family alike were devastated by the news of her death.
聽到她去世的噩耗，無論家人還是朋友都悲痛欲絕。

NONE: › the parts of the body that food goes through as it is eaten and digested
消化道
› a regular amount of money that a law court orders a person to pay to his or her partner after a divorce (= the legal ending of a marriage)
（離婚後法院判決一方支付給另一方的）贍養費，生活費

C: › specialized science an amount taken from a larger quantity, so that it can be tested, etc.
› specialized mathematics a quantity that can be divided into another quantity an exact number of times

after verb: B1 [ after verb ] living, not dead
C2 If something is alive, it continues to exist.

example: He must be 90 if he's still alive.
如果他還在世的話，肯定有90歲了。
Doctors kept him alive on a life-support machine.
醫生使用維生系統來維持他的生命。
She's alive and well and living in New Zealand.
她生活得很好，目前住在紐西蘭。
Relatives of the missing sailors are struggling to keep their hopes alive.
失蹤水手的親人仍然苦守著他們能生還的希望。

NONE: › If you are alive to something, you are thinking about it or familiar with it.
意識到，認識到；注意到

example: I ski for the excitement, but I'm also always alive to the risks.
我滑雪是為了追求刺激，但是我也從沒有忘記這項運動的風險。

NONE: › full of things that are living and moving
充滿，滿是，到處都是（有生命的或活動的東西）

example: The pond was alive with frogs.
池塘裡到處都是青蛙。
